archetype.name: Pocket Passer (volume-fed)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who wins from the pocket on short and intermediate timing routes, rarely leaves it, and whose big counting stats come mostly from how often a losing team asks him to throw.

report.headline: Top-three volume, middle-of-the-pack efficiency: the trailing script is doing the lifting.
report.take:
Shough ranks 3rd in passing yards and passing touchdowns, which looks like a breakout. His efficiency says otherwise. At 0.036 EPA per dropback (24th of 42) and 6.96 adjusted net yards per dropback (22nd), he is almost exactly the quarterback he was as a rookie, when he posted 0.025 EPA per play and ranked 34th of 65. The difference is volume. He has thrown 180 times in four games, the Saints pass 2.4 points more than expected in neutral situations (8th), and a defense ranked 30th in EPA and last against the run has given up 31, 35 and 45 points in three of those games. His 410-yard opener came against a defense now ranked 32nd and still finished at -1.0 EPA.

The passing profile is a real one. He works the short and intermediate areas on time. His 10-19 yard throws are the best part of his game: 0.648 EPA per attempt with a 9.6 CPOE on 36 attempts. His bad-throw rate has fallen from 15.3% last year to 10%, and his aggressiveness has risen from 12.8% to 17.2%, so he is throwing into tighter windows and missing less often. That is real development. Chris Olave is the main beneficiary at 0.73 EPA per target on 48 targets.

The weak spots are the drive killers, and they cancel out much of that progress. He gets pressured on only 15.3% of dropbacks (6th lowest), but when pressure arrives it turns into a sack 34.5% of the time (28th of 32). The rookie number was worse at 41.9%, 50th of 64, so this is how he plays rather than a bad month. He is not a scrambler: 3% of dropbacks become scrambles, so he doesn't escape trouble and gain yards to offset the sacks. Add 3 lost fumbles (40th of 42) on 5 turnover-worthy fumbles and a -0.128 EPA on third down with 5 sacks in 48 plays. A lot of the good work disappears before it shows up on the scoreboard.

Going forward, the yardage will hold up as long as the defense keeps forcing shootouts. The touchdown rate will not. Eight of his 9 touchdowns came in the red zone on short throws, 8 scores on 27 red-zone attempts, and that pace on this efficiency won't last. Expect the counting stats to come down toward his underlying level of roughly a league-average passer. That decline starts this week against the league's best defense.

strengths.title: Intermediate timing throws
strengths.body: Between 10 and 19 air yards he has been excellent: 0.648 EPA per attempt, a 64% success rate and a 9.6 CPOE. This is where his accuracy and his trust in Olave meet. On 36 attempts it is a meaningful sample but not a settled one. The drop in his bad-throw rate from last year suggests at least part of it is genuine growth.

strengths.title: Accuracy improving as aggressiveness rises
strengths.body: He is throwing into tight windows more often than as a rookie (17.2% vs 12.8%) while completing more than expected (4.25 CPOE, 13th) and missing less often. Usually aggressiveness costs a passer some accuracy. His didn't, and that is the clearest sign of development in the dossier.

strengths.title: Volume he can count on
strengths.body: A pass-leaning offense paired with a bottom-three defense means he will keep throwing 40 or more times most weeks. That is why he ranks 3rd in passing yards with an efficiency profile in the 20s. The volume is tied to the team's situation rather than his skill, and it lasts as long as the defense keeps giving up points.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: Pressure doesn't reach him often, but when it does he goes down roughly a third of the time. He doesn't buy time with his legs, so the sacks bring no scrambles in return. The same weakness showed up even more strongly in 2025, which makes it a real flaw rather than noise. It matters most against fronts that win quickly.

concerns.title: Fumbles and third-down stalls
concerns.body: Three lost fumbles in four games, two of them against Las Vegas, come from five turnover-worthy fumbles, so they are not just bad bounces. On third down he averages -0.128 EPA, faces 7.7 yards to go on average and has taken 5 sacks. The fumble count should cool somewhat, but the ball-security issue is real.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate ahead of efficiency
concerns.body: He has 8 red-zone touchdowns on 27 attempts, and 8 of his 9 scores came on short throws. That pace is far ahead of an offense that ranks 19th in pass EPA. The screen game behind the line is also costing him: -0.27 EPA across 26 attempts. Expect touchdowns to fall back toward roughly one and a half to two per game.

trend.note: His EPA has swung from -1.0 to 10.9, then -3.6, then 0.7. The one strong game came at Baltimore on a short, quick-game plan (5.4 intended air yards). The two worst came with turnovers attached. Week 4 against Atlanta was the most aggressive game he has played (25% aggressiveness, 10.2 intended air yards) and produced only modest results.

nextGame.headline: Best pass rush in football meets his worst habit under pressure
nextGame.body:
Minnesota ranks 1st in defensive EPA, pass EPA, success rate, hit rate (25.5%) and sack rate (10.5%). It allows the fewest fantasy points (10.5 PPR a game) and touchdowns to quarterbacks. Shough's numbers look reasonable partly because he has rarely been pressured. This front should pressure him well above his 15.3% rate, and his 34.5% pressure-to-sack rate means drives will end. The Vikings' relative soft spot is deep, where they rank 12th, while they are 7th on short throws. That pushes him toward the 20-plus-yard throws he completes only 37.5% of the time.

Availability favors him only indirectly. Minnesota's offense was already 28th in EPA and last in success rate. It is now without Justin Jefferson and guard Donovan Jackson, with left tackle Christian Darrisaw in concussion protocol. That makes it less likely the Saints' defense falls behind early, which also takes away the trailing volume that has inflated his stats. On his side, Travis Etienne is on IR until November and Jordyn Tyson won't return before Week 7. That leaves Bryce Lance (-0.655 EPA per target) in the rotation and the backfield receiving work with Alvin Kamara (-0.293). Noah Fant's return date lines up with this game, which would give him another tight end option behind Juwan Johnson.

keyMatchups.title: Vikings pass rush vs. his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota leads the league in both hit rate and sack rate, and the Saints' line is merely average at allowing hits (15th). He has taken 12 sacks in four games against easier fronts. This is the clearest matchup edge on the board, and it runs against him.

keyMatchups.title: Olave vs. a defense built to stop short throws
keyMatchups.body: Olave has been his outlet, at 0.73 EPA per target on 48 targets. Minnesota's short-area defense ranks 7th, while it is 12th deep. If the quick game is taken away, he needs Olave on intermediate and deep throws, which is where he is most accurate and where the Vikings bend slightly more.

keyMatchups.title: Game script without the shootout
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota's offense is last in success rate and passes 5 points less than expected, and its injuries hit its best receiver and its line. A slower, lower-scoring game cuts into the passing volume that has carried his production.

nextGame.watch: Early third-and-long snaps: if he is holding the ball against the Vikings' four-man rush and taking sacks, the afternoon is decided by halftime.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts that should hold are his volume, his short-to-intermediate accuracy and the lower bad-throw rate, all backed by visible development since 2025. The parts that should regress are his touchdown rate and possibly his fumble count. Nine touchdowns from a passer at 0.036 EPA per dropback, eight of them inside the red zone, is a hot streak. The yardage pace of about 301 a game is propped up by a 410-yard opener and by a defense that forces him to chase games.

Sack-proneness is the long-term limit on his ceiling. It is now two seasons old, and without much scramble value to offset it, it caps his efficiency at roughly league average. Tyson's possible return around Week 7 and Etienne's in November would improve the supporting cast, since the third receiver and the backfield are currently dragging down his production. Expect a 250-plus-yard passer with fewer touchdowns, stronger in shootouts and weak against good pass rushes.
swingFactors: Whether the Saints' defense keeps forcing shootouts
Jordyn Tyson's return replacing Bryce Lance's targets

bets.reason: Minnesota leads the league in both sack rate (10.5%) and hit rate, and he turns 34.5% of pressures into sacks, a habit that was worse in 2025. He took 12 sacks against weaker fronts.
The Vikings allow 0.75 passing TDs a game to quarterbacks, fewest in the league. His own touchdown rate rests on an unsustainable 8 red-zone scores on 27 attempts.

His average is lifted by a 410-yard game against the league's worst defense. Minnesota allows 237.3 yards a game to quarterbacks. A weakened Vikings offense also makes a heavy-trailing script less likely.

Minnesota's offense ranks 28th in EPA and last in success rate. It now plays without Jefferson and Donovan Jackson, with Darrisaw questionable, and passes well below expectation. The Saints' bad defense is the risk, since it pushed three of four games over.

confidence.note: Four-game sample, but his efficiency and sack profile match a 10-game 2025 season.
